verses.1:1: And it happened, after Israel was brought into captivity and Jerusalem was deserted, that Jeremiah the prophet sat weeping, and lamented with this lamentation over Jerusalem; and sighing and wailing with a bitter spirit, he said, Aleph: "How alone the city sits, full of people! The mistress of the nations has become like a widow; the princess of the provinces has come under tribute.
verses.1:2: Beth: Weeping, she wept in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks; from among all her dear ones there is no one to comfort her; all her friends have spurned her and have become enemies to her.
verses.1:3: Gimel: Judah has departed because of affliction and the abundance of servitude; she has lived among the nations and has not found rest; all her pursuers have seized her in the midst of straits.
verses.1:4: Daleth: The roads of Zion mourn because there are none who come to the festival; all her gates are destroyed, her priests are groaning, her virgins are unkempt, and she herself is oppressed with bitterness.
verses.1:5: He: Her foes have come to be at the head; her enemies have grown wealthy, for the Lord has spoken against her because of the multitude of her iniquities. Her little ones have been led into captivity before the face of the oppressor.
verses.1:6: Vav: And all her beauty has gone out from the daughter of Zion; her princes have become like rams finding no pasture, and they have gone away without strength before the face of the pursuer.
verses.1:7: Zayin: Jerusalem has remembered the days of her affliction and transgression, all her treasured things that she had possessed from ancient days, when her people fell into a hostile hand and there was no helper; the foes saw her and mocked her sabbaths.
verses.1:8: Heth: Jerusalem has sinned a sin; therefore she has become unstable. All who glorified her have spurned her, because they have seen her disgrace; she herself, however, groaning, has turned backward.
verses.1:9: Teth: Her filth is on her feet, and she has not remembered her end; she has been brought down severely, having no comforter. See, Lord, my affliction, for the enemy has lifted himself up.
verses.1:10: Yod: The foe has stretched out his hand to all her treasured things, for she has seen the nations enter her sanctuary, concerning whom You had commanded that they should not enter Your assembly.
verses.1:11: Kaph: All her people are groaning and seeking bread; they have given every precious thing for food to revive the soul. See, Lord, and consider that I have become worthless!
verses.1:12: Lamed: All you who pass along the road, pay attention and see if there is sorrow like my sorrow! For He has harvested me, as the Lord has spoken, on the day of the wrath of His fury.
verses.1:13: Mem: From on high He has sent fire into my bones and has instructed me; He has spread a net for my feet, He has turned me backward; He has made me desolate, worn out with grief all day long.
verses.1:14: Nun: The yoke of my iniquities has kept watch; in His hand they have been twisted together and placed upon my neck. My strength has been weakened; the Lord has given me into a hand from which I will not be able to rise.
verses.1:15: Samekh: The Lord has taken away all my noble ones from my midst; He has summoned a time against me to crush my chosen ones. The Lord has trodden the winepress for the virgin daughter of Judah.
verses.1:16: Ayin: For this reason I am weeping, and my eye is pouring down waters, because a comforter who restores my soul has been removed far from me. My children have been ruined, because the enemy has prevailed.
verses.1:17: Pe: Zion has spread out her hands; there is no one to comfort her. The Lord has commanded against Jacob his foes around him; Jerusalem has become like one defiled by menstruation among them.
verses.1:18: Tsade: The Lord is righteous, for I have provoked His mouth to anger. Hear, I implore you, all peoples, and see my sorrow: my virgins and my young men have gone away into captivity.
verses.1:19: Qoph: I called my friends, and they themselves deceived me; my priests and my elders have been consumed in the city, because they sought food for themselves to revive their soul.
verses.1:20: Resh: See, Lord, that I am in distress: my belly is in turmoil, my heart is overturned within myself, for I am full of bitterness. Outside the sword has killed, and at home death is like it.
verses.1:21: Shin: They have heard that I groan and that there is no one to comfort me; all my enemies have heard of my calamity and have rejoiced because You have done it. You have brought the day of consolation, and they will become like me.
verses.1:22: Tav: Let all their wickedness come before You, and harvest them just as You have harvested me because of all my iniquities; for my groans are many, and my heart is grieving."
verses.2:1: Aleph: How the Lord has covered the daughter of Zion with darkness in His fury! He has cast down from heaven to earth the glorious one of Israel, and has not remembered the footstool of His feet on the day of His fury!
verses.2:2: Beth: The Lord has overthrown, and has not spared, all the lovely things of Jacob; in His fury He has destroyed the strongholds of the virgin of Judah and thrown them down to the ground; He has defiled the kingdom and its princes.
verses.2:3: Gimel: In the wrath of His fury He has shattered every horn of Israel; He has turned His right hand backward from the face of the enemy, and He has kindled in Jacob, as it were, a fire of a devouring flame all around.
verses.2:4: Daleth: He has bent His bow like an enemy, He has steadied His right hand like a foe, and He has killed everything that was beautiful to look at in the tabernacle of the daughter of Zion; He has poured out His indignation like fire.
verses.2:5: He: The Lord has become like an enemy; He has overthrown Israel. He has overthrown all its ramparts, He has laid waste its strongholds, and He has filled the daughter of Judah with the humiliated man and the humiliated woman.
verses.2:6: Vav: And He has laid waste His tent like a garden; He has demolished His tabernacle. The Lord has handed over to oblivion in Zion festival and sabbath, and to reproach and to the indignation of His fury, king and priest.
verses.2:7: Zayin: The Lord has rejected His altar; He has cursed His holy place; He has handed over into the hand of the enemy the walls of her towers. They have raised their voice in the house of the Lord as on a festival day.
verses.2:8: Heth: The Lord has planned to lay waste the wall of the daughter of Zion; He has stretched out His line and has not turned His hand away from destruction; and the outer wall has mourned, and the wall has been laid waste together with it.
verses.2:9: Teth: Her gates have sunk into the ground; He has ruined and crushed her bars; her king and her princes are among the nations. There is no law, and her prophets have not found a vision from the Lord.
verses.2:10: Yod: The elders of the daughter of Zion have sat on the ground, they have kept silent; they have sprinkled their heads with ashes, they have bound themselves with sackcloth; the virgins of Jerusalem have cast their heads down to the ground.
verses.2:11: Kaph: My eyes have failed from tears, my inward parts are in turmoil; my liver has been poured out on the ground over the shattering of the daughter of my people, while the little one and the nursing infant fainted in the streets of the town.
verses.2:12: Lamed: They said to their mothers, "Where is wheat and wine?" as they fainted like the wounded in the streets of the city, as they breathed out their souls in the bosom of their mothers.
verses.2:13: Mem: To what shall I compare you, or to what shall I liken you, daughter of Jerusalem? To what shall I equate you and comfort you, virgin, daughter of Zion? For your shattering is as great as the sea; who will heal you?
verses.2:14: Nun: Your prophets have seen false and foolish things for you, and they did not expose your iniquity so as to provoke you to repentance; instead, they have seen for you false oracles and expulsions.
verses.2:15: Samekh: All who pass along the road have clapped their hands over you; they have hissed and shaken their head over the daughter of Jerusalem, saying, "Is this the city of perfect beauty, the joy of the whole earth?"
verses.2:16: Pe: All your enemies have opened their mouth against you; they have hissed and gnashed their teeth, and said, "We will devour her! Look, this is the day that we were waiting for; we have found it, we have seen it."
verses.2:17: Ayin: The Lord has done what He planned; He has fulfilled His word, which He had commanded from ancient days; He has destroyed and has not spared, and He has made the enemy rejoice over you, and He has exalted the horn of your foes.
verses.2:18: Tsade: Their heart cried out to the Lord upon the walls of the daughter of Zion. Pour down tears like a torrent through day and night; do not give yourself rest, and let the pupil of your eye not keep silent.
verses.2:19: Qoph: Rise up, give praise in the night, at the beginning of the watches; pour out your heart like water before the presence of the Lord; lift up your hands to Him for the soul of your little ones, who have fainted in hunger at the head of all the crossroads.
verses.2:20: Resh: See, Lord, and consider whom You have harvested in this way. Will women really eat their fruit, little ones the measure of a palm? Are priest and prophet killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
verses.2:21: Shin: The boy and the old man have lain on the ground outside; my virgins and my young men have fallen by the sword. You have killed on the day of Your fury; You have struck down and have not shown mercy.
verses.2:22: Tav: You have called, as to a festival day, those who would terrify me from all around; and on the day of the fury of the Lord there was no one who escaped or was left behind. Those whom I brought up and nourished, my enemy has consumed them.
verses.3:1: Aleph: I am the man who sees my poverty under the rod of His indignation.
verses.3:2: Aleph: He has driven me and led me into darkness, and not into light.
verses.3:3: Aleph: Against me alone He turns His hand and turns it again all day long.
verses.3:4: Beth: He has made my skin and my flesh grow old; He has crushed my bones.
verses.3:5: Beth: He has built all around me and surrounded me with gall and toil.
verses.3:6: Beth: In dark places He has settled me, like those eternally dead.
verses.3:7: Gimel: He has built against me on every side so that I may not go out; He has weighed down my shackle.
verses.3:8: Gimel: Yet even when I cry out and plead, He has shut out my prayer.
verses.3:9: Gimel: He has closed off my ways with squared stones; He has overturned my paths.
verses.3:10: Daleth: He has become to me a bear lying in ambush, a lion in hidden places.
verses.3:11: Daleth: He has overturned my paths and shattered me; He has left me desolate.
verses.3:12: Daleth: He has drawn His bow and placed me as a target for the arrow.
verses.3:13: He: He has sent the daughters of His quiver into my kidneys.
verses.3:14: He: I have become a mockery to all my people, their song all day long.
verses.3:15: He: He has filled me with bitternesses; He has intoxicated me with wormwood.
verses.3:16: Vav: And He has broken my teeth by number; He has fed me ashes.
verses.3:17: Vav: And my soul has been thrust away from peace; I have forgotten good things.
verses.3:18: Vav: And I said, "My end has perished, and my hope from the Lord."
verses.3:19: Zayin: Remember my poverty and my transgression, wormwood and gall.
verses.3:20: Zayin: I will surely remember, and my soul will waste away within me.
verses.3:21: Zayin: Recalling these things in my heart, I will therefore hope.
verses.3:25: Teth: The Lord is good to those who hope in Him, to the soul seeking Him.
verses.3:26: Teth: It is good to await in silence the salvation of God.
verses.3:27: Teth: It is good for a man when he bears a yoke from his youth.
verses.3:28: Yod: He will sit alone and keep silent, because he has lifted it upon himself.
verses.3:30: Yod: He will give his cheek to the one striking him; he will be sated with reproaches.
verses.3:31: Kaph: For the Lord will not reject for eternity.
verses.3:32: Kaph: For if He has cast away, He will also show compassion, according to the multitude of His mercies.
verses.3:33: Kaph: For not from His heart has He humbled and cast away the sons of men.
verses.3:34: Lamed: To crush under one's feet all the prisoners of the earth.
verses.3:35: Lamed: To turn aside a man's justice in the sight of the face of the Most High.
verses.3:36: Lamed: To subvert a man in his case; the Lord did not know.
verses.3:37: Mem: Who is this who spoke so that it came to be, without the Lord commanding?
verses.3:38: Mem: From the mouth of the Most High, will not both evil things and good things come out?
verses.3:39: Mem: Why has a living person grumbled, a man for his sins?
verses.3:40: Nun: Let us examine our ways and investigate, and let us return to the Lord.
verses.3:41: Nun: Let us lift our hearts together with our hands to the Lord in the heavens.
verses.3:42: Nun: We have acted wickedly and provoked You to anger; for this reason You are inexorable.
verses.3:43: Samekh: You have covered us in fury and struck us; You have killed and not spared.
verses.3:44: Samekh: You have placed a cloud before Yourself so that prayer may not pass through.
verses.3:45: Samekh: You have made me an uprooting and a casting away in the midst of the peoples.
verses.3:46: Pe: All the enemies have opened their mouth against us.
verses.3:47: Pe: Dread and a snare have come upon us, prophecy and crushing.
verses.3:48: Pe: My eye has poured down streams of waters at the crushing of the daughter of my people.
verses.3:49: Ayin: My eye was afflicted and did not keep silent, because there was no rest.
verses.3:50: Ayin: Until the Lord should look down and see from the heavens.
verses.3:51: Ayin: My eye has plundered my soul on account of all the daughters of my city.
verses.3:52: Tsade: By hunting, my enemies caught me like a bird, without cause.
verses.3:53: Tsade: My life slipped into the pit, and they placed a stone over me.
verses.3:54: Tsade: Waters flooded over my head; I said, "I have perished."
verses.3:55: Qoph: I called upon Your name, Lord, from the deepest pit.
verses.3:56: Qoph: You heard my voice; do not turn Your ear away from my sobbing and cries.
verses.3:57: Qoph: You drew near on the day when I called upon You; You said, "Do not be afraid."
verses.3:58: Resh: You have judged, Lord, the cause of my soul, Redeemer of my life.
verses.3:59: Resh: You have seen, Lord, their injustice against me; judge my case.
verses.3:60: Resh: You have seen all their fury, all their thoughts against me.
verses.3:61: Shin: You have heard their reproach, Lord, all their thoughts against me.
verses.3:62: Shin: The lips of those rising up against me, and their meditations against me all day long.
verses.3:63: Shin: See their sitting and their rising; I am their psalm.
verses.3:64: Tav: You will repay them in kind, Lord, according to the works of their hands.
verses.3:65: Tav: You will give them a shield of the heart, Your toil.
verses.3:66: Tav: You will pursue them in fury and crush them under the heavens, Lord.
verses.4:1: Aleph: How the gold has been darkened, the finest color changed! The stones of the sanctuary have been scattered at the head of all the streets!
verses.4:2: Beth: The sons of Zion, renowned and clothed in choicest gold, how they have been counted as earthenware vessels, the work of a potter's hands!
verses.4:3: Gimel: Yet even the lamias have bared the breast; they have nursed their young. The daughter of my people is cruel, like an ostrich in the desert.
verses.4:4: Daleth: The tongue of the nursing infant has clung to its palate in thirst; the small children asked for bread, and there was no one to break it for them.
verses.4:5: He: Those who dined luxuriously have perished in the roads; those who were raised in saffron garments have embraced dung.
verses.4:6: Vav: And the iniquity of the daughter of my people has become greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment, and no hands laid hold in her.
verses.4:7: Zayin: Her Nazirites were whiter than snow, brighter than milk, ruddier than ancient ivory, more beautiful than sapphire.
verses.4:8: Heth: Their face has grown blacker than coals, and they are not recognized in the streets; their skin has clung to their bones; it has dried up and become like wood.
verses.4:9: Teth: It was better for those struck down by the sword than for those killed by famine, for these wasted away, consumed by the barrenness of the land.
verses.4:10: Yod: The hands of merciful women cooked their own children; they became their food in the crushing of the daughter of my people.
verses.4:11: Kaph: The Lord has completed His fury; He has poured out the wrath of His indignation, and He has kindled a fire in Zion, and it has devoured its foundations.
verses.4:12: Lamed: The kings of the earth and all the inhabitants of the world did not believe that a foe and an enemy would enter through the gates of Jerusalem.
verses.4:13: Mem: Because of the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests, who poured out the blood of the righteous in her midst.
verses.4:14: Nun: They wandered blind in the streets; they were defiled with blood, and when they could not, they held their hems.
verses.4:15: Samekh: "Stand back, defiled ones!" they shouted to them. "Stand back, go away, do not touch!" For indeed they quarreled, and shaken, they said among the nations, "He will no longer dwell among them."
verses.4:16: Pe: The face of the Lord has divided them; He will no longer look upon them. They had no reverence for the faces of the priests, nor did they have mercy on the elders.
verses.4:17: Ayin: While we still held out, our eyes failed for our futile help, as we looked intently toward a nation that could not save.
verses.4:18: Tsade: Our footsteps slipped along the path of our streets; our end has drawn near; our days are completed, for our end has come.
verses.4:19: Qoph: Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of the sky; over the mountains they pursued us; in the desert they lay in wait for us.
verses.4:20: Resh: The breath of our mouth, the anointed Lord, was captured in our sins, to whom we said, "In Your shadow we will live among the nations."
verses.4:21: Shin: Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz! The cup will reach you as well; you will become drunk and be laid bare.
verses.4:22: Tav: Your iniquity is completed, daughter of Zion; He will no longer send you into exile. He has visited your iniquity, daughter of Edom; He has uncovered your sins.
verses.5:1: Remember, Lord, what has happened to us; look closely and regard our reproach.
verses.5:2: Our inheritance has been turned over to outsiders, our houses to foreigners.
verses.5:3: We have been made orphans, without a father; our mothers are like widows.
verses.5:4: We have drunk our water for money; we have purchased our wood at a price.
verses.5:5: We were driven by our necks; no rest was given to the weary.
verses.5:6: We gave our hand to Egypt and to the Assyrians, so that we might be filled with bread.
verses.5:7: Our fathers sinned and are no more, and we have carried their iniquities.
verses.5:8: Slaves have ruled over us; there was no one to redeem us from their hand.
verses.5:9: At the peril of our lives we brought bread for ourselves, because of the sword in the desert.
verses.5:10: Our skin has been scorched like an oven, because of the storms of famine.
verses.5:11: They humiliated the women in Zion, and the virgins in the cities of Judah.
verses.5:12: Princes were hanged by the hand; they had no reverence for the faces of the elders.
verses.5:13: They shamelessly abused the young men, and the boys collapsed on the wood.
verses.5:14: The elders are gone from the gates, the young men from the choir of musicians.
verses.5:15: The joy of our heart has failed; our dance has been turned into mourning.
verses.5:16: The crown of our head has fallen; woe to us, because we have sinned!
verses.5:17: Because of this our heart has grown sorrowful; for this reason our eyes have been darkened,
verses.5:18: on account of Mount Zion, because it has perished; foxes have walked on it.
verses.5:19: But You, Lord, will remain forever, Your throne from generation to generation.
verses.5:20: Why will You forget us forever, abandon us for the length of days?
verses.5:21: Turn us back, Lord, to Yourself, and we will be turned back; renew our days as from the beginning.
verses.5:22: But casting us away, You have rejected us; You have been fiercely angry against us.

notes.1:1: Following the Septuagint, the Vulgate includes the opening historical preface attributing the lament to Jeremiah; this preface is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text. The Hebrew alphabet letter names (Aleph through Tav) at the head of each verse reflect the acrostic structure preserved in the Latin text.
notes.1:5: Vulgate "locutus est super eam" ("has spoken against her"; so also "locutus est" in 1:12) reflects a reading of the Hebrew verb as speaking rather than the Masoretic Text's "has afflicted her".
notes.1:7: Vulgate "praevaricationis" ("transgression") and "sabbata ejus" ("her sabbaths") are distinctive Latin renderings where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "wandering" and "her downfall"; similarly in 1:6 Vulgate "arietes" ("rams") contrasts with Hebrew "stags", and in 1:9 "in pedibus ejus" ("on her feet") contrasts with Hebrew "in her skirts".
notes.1:12: Vulgate "vindemiavit" ("has harvested"; also in 1:22 and 2:20) literally denotes harvesting grapes at the vintage, rendering the Hebrew verb that can mean either "to glean a vineyard" or "to deal severely with".
notes.1:21: Vulgate "adduxisti diem consolationis" ("You have brought the day of consolation") is a notable Vulgate-distinct reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Bring the day You have announced"; see also "Vigilavit" ("has kept watch") in 1:14 and "amaritudine plena sum" ("I am full of bitterness") in 1:20.
notes.2:5: Vulgate "humiliatum et humiliatam" ("the humiliated man and the humiliated woman") mirrors a Hebrew rhyming pair ("mourning and lamentation") by rendering it from the related Hebrew root for humiliation.
notes.2:14: Vulgate "ut te ad poenitentiam provocarent" ("so as to provoke you to repentance") interprets the Hebrew phrase for restoring fortunes in a spiritual sense; "assumptiones ... et ejectiones" ("oracles and expulsions") reflects Jerome's understanding of the Hebrew terms for prophetic burdens and banishments.
notes.2:16: In chapter 2, the Vulgate preserves the Hebrew acrostic's reversal of Pe (2:16) and Ayin (2:17) compared with chapter 1; Vulgate future "Devorabimus" ("We will devour") contrasts with the Hebrew perfect ("We have swallowed her up").
notes.2:18: Vulgate "super muros filiae Sion" ("upon the walls of the daughter of Zion") takes the phrase adverbially rather than as the Masoretic Text's vocative ("O wall of the daughter of Zion"); in 2:19 Vulgate "lauda" ("give praise") renders a Hebrew imperative meaning either "cry out" or "praise".
notes.2:20: Vulgate "parvulos ad mensuram palmae" ("little ones the measure of a palm") describes tiny infants only a handbreadth long, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to children tenderly cared for.
notes.3:1: In the Clementine Vulgate, the Hebrew acrostic letter names appear inline before every verse of Lamentations 3 (rendered here in standard modern English spelling). The Vulgate also reads paupertatem meam ("my poverty"), whereas the Hebrew reads "affliction."
notes.3:16: The Vulgate distinctively reads ad numerum ("by number," i.e., tooth by tooth) and cibavit me cinere ("He has fed me ashes"), where the Hebrew reads "with gravel" and "He has made me cower in ashes."
notes.3:18: The Vulgate translates Hebrew netzach ("endurance" or "strength") as finis meus ("my end"), reflecting its standard rendering of that root elsewhere in the Vulgate.
notes.3:19: The Vulgate reads transgressionis meae ("my transgression"), whereas the Hebrew term is generally understood as "my wandering" or "my homelessness."
notes.3:28: The Vulgate uses the reflexive levavit super se ("he has lifted it upon himself," referring to the yoke of v. 27), differing from the Hebrew phrasing commonly understood as "because He [God] has laid it on him."
notes.3:36: The Vulgate reads Dominus ignoravit ("the Lord did not know"), rendering Hebrew lo' ra'ah ("does not see/approve") with "not knowing" in the biblical sense of refusing to recognize or countenance the injustices of vv. 34-36.
notes.3:45: The Clementine Vulgate reads singular posuisti me ("You have made me") with eradicationem ("an uprooting"), whereas the Hebrew reads plural "You have made us offscouring/scum."
notes.3:47: The Vulgate distinctively reads vaticinatio ("prophecy") and laqueus ("a snare"), where the Hebrew reads "devastation" and "pitfall."
notes.3:58: The Vulgate reads the noun redemptor vitae meae ("Redeemer of my life") alongside Judicasti ("You have judged"), whereas the Hebrew has verbal forms rendered "You have pleaded" and "You have redeemed my life."
notes.3:65: The Vulgate translates Hebrew meginnat-lev ("hardness/dullness of heart") literally as scutum cordis ("a shield of the heart"), and reads laborem tuum ("Your toil") where the Hebrew reads "Your curse."
notes.4:3: Latin lamiae refers to legendary child-devouring monsters (or sea monsters), where the Hebrew refers to jackals; the Clementine Vulgate also preserves the Hebrew acrostic letter names at the head of each verse in chapter 4, with Pe (4:16) preceding Ayin (4:17).
notes.4:7: Vulgate "Nazirites" (Nazaraei) and "ancient ivory" (ebore antiquo) preserve distinctive renderings where the Hebrew is commonly translated "princes" (or "consecrated ones") and "corals" (or "rubies").
notes.4:14: Vulgate "when they could not, they held their hems" (cumque non possent, tenuerunt lacinias suas) is a distinctive Latin rendering of a difficult Hebrew clause usually understood as "so that no one could touch their garments."
notes.4:15: Vulgate "they quarreled" (jurgati sunt) and the singular "He will no longer dwell among them" (Non addet ultra ut habitet in eis, referring to the Lord) differ from the Hebrew, which uses plural verbs referring to the exiles ("they fled" and "they shall stay no longer").
notes.4:20: Latin christus Dominus ("the anointed Lord") sets the two nouns in apposition, as the Septuagint does (christos kyrios), where the Hebrew reads "the anointed of the Lord"; the Vulgate also reads oris nostri ("of our mouth") and in peccatis nostris ("in our sins") where the Hebrew has "of our nostrils" and "in their pits."
notes.5:5: Latin minabamur is the passive of Late Latin minare ("to drive," as of livestock or captives), conveying being driven harshly by the neck, where the Hebrew reads "our pursuers are at our necks."
notes.5:10: Vulgate "storms of famine" (tempestatum famis) renders a rare Hebrew phrase usually understood as "burning heat" or "raging fever of famine."
notes.5:13: Vulgate "They shamelessly abused the young men" (Adolescentibus impudice abusi sunt) follows an ancient euphemistic interpretation of Hebrew "young men bore the millstone," and "on the wood" (in ligno) literally reflects Hebrew "under [loads of] wood."
notes.5:22: Vulgate renders the closing verse as a stark declarative contrast ("But casting us away, You have rejected us," Sed projiciens repulisti nos), whereas the Hebrew conjunction is often taken conditionally as "unless You have utterly rejected us."

unplaced.text: Heth: It is through the mercies of the Lord that we have not been consumed, because His compassions have not failed.
Heth: They are new at daybreak; Your faithfulness is great.
unplaced.note: Latin "Novi" ("new," masculine plural) has no expressed noun and is taken as referring back to the Lord's mercies and compassions in the preceding verse, although misericordiae and miserationes are feminine; "diluculo" is singular ("at daybreak").

unplaced.text: Heth: "The Lord is my portion," my soul has said; therefore I will wait for Him.
Yod: He will put his mouth in the dust, if perhaps there may be hope.
